analysis.title: JPMorgan Co-Head Of Trading: Market Finally Focusing On AI Circularity
key_insights: JPM Market Intel (Andrew Tyler) keeps its Tactical Bullish call on the S&P despite the October drawdown and the Nasdaq's worst plunge since Covid, which erased all YTD gains for tech funds. The S&P had its biggest drop since Liberation Day.

Rebound argument: when the NDX is within ~6% of its all-time high and falls 3.5%+ in a day, it has tended to rebound ~3% the following week. The effect is stronger when the decline falls on a Friday, which JPM reads as de-grossing rather than a change in fundamental views.

JPM argues this week's data can ease stagflation and recession fears tied to an AI capex decline. Its support: record household net worth, checking balances up about 5x since COVID, room to add debt based on debt service as a share of disposable income, and credit card delinquencies and charge-offs not yet back to pre-COVID levels.

JPM expects businesses to avoid margin compression because public company margins are at or near records and would need to compress before mass layoffs begin. It says AI is not a significant driver of hiring and that CRWV employs only about 550 people.

JPM sees the main AI-slowdown effect as capex declines (a hit to GDP growth, not necessarily to labor markets or spending) and possible hyperscaler layoffs. The main consumer risk is a negative wealth effect from a bear market. A rising share of spending is funded by consumers selling investment accounts.

The biggest non-AI risk JPM names is a re-escalation in the Middle East. Per a WSJ report cited in the note, Iran damaged US regional bases and munitions are depleted, so a new round of US attacks could be limited in scope and duration and could prompt diplomacy. JPM says oil already prices this outcome, which limits upside for energy, bond yields and equity downside.
Seasonality: November is the strongest month on average this century, and post-midterm seasonality is a tailwind.

Ron Adler (JPM Global Co-Head of Cash Trading) says AI is the fulcrum of the market. Investors held hyperscaler longs for years, then moved further out the risk curve into picks-and-shovels names as hyperscalers began funding ambitions through capital markets rather than capex. He says circular AI financing did not get enough scrutiny while markets rose, and that has changed.
Adler lists stress points: META raising money at 7.5%, a Chinese chipmaker putting its IPO on hold, MRVL down about 40% after the LITE deal announcement, and hedge fund stress.

Adler says the midterm election may have tipped the AI trade. He expects the election outcome to make data center growth harder (citing META comments) and that this is hitting photonics/optics, memory and neoclouds. He calls gridlock potentially good, but says unknowns remain and rhetoric will intensify.

Crowding remains a pain point. HF long/short spreads are working, client questions on pain levels, factors, correlations, unwinding and fund stress are rising, and JPM cash volumes are up 50% after a busy post-election session. Adler does not expect many to rush in to defend dips outside defensives.

Adler says the flows look directionally rational but the magnitude is the surprise, and part of the move is indiscriminate portfolio-pain selling. A lot of positioning pain has been taken, and a harder path for datacenter expansion could ease pressure on capital markets and yields.

sector_views.rationale: JPM Market Intel expects tech to stabilize and a broadening trend to lift the SPX. Adler describes AI-linked picks-and-shovels names (photonics/optics, memory, neoclouds) as under stress from circular financing concerns and a harder path for data center expansion.
Adler expects few buyers to defend the selloff outside defensives.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports JPM's view that the consumer can absorb an AI capex decline without a recession.
Cash buffers are historically strong, which supports spending.

macro_indicators.reading: Not yet fully normalized to pre-COVID levels
macro_indicators.interpretation: Credit is not showing consumer stress, and there is room to add debt.
Margins would need to compress before mass layoffs begin.
Client activity is high, matching anxiety about unwinding and fund stress.

trade_ideas.rationale: A near-term rebound after a flush, a broadening trend, tech stabilization, easing recession fears and positive November seasonality.
trade_ideas.risk: Further AI circular-financing stress, capex declines, a Middle East re-escalation, and continued crowding unwinds.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM Market Intel argues the Friday flush will be followed by a rebound of about 3% in the NDX, driven by de-grossing, a broadening trend, tech stabilization, a resilient consumer and positive November seasonality.
tension_points.bear_case: Adler (JPM cash trading) says AI circular financing is now under scrutiny, with META raising money at 7.5%, a Chinese chipmaker IPO on hold, MRVL down ~40% and hedge fund stress. Few buyers are expected to defend the dip outside defensives.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further stress in AI-related capital raising, or a rebound failing to appear after the Friday flush.

theme_stances.key_argument: Circular AI revenues got the airtime, but the circular impact of AI on markets and tech did not get enough scrutiny while things were going well.
